guard: every tool handed pi.registerTool is a closed object whose JSON round-trip carries only JSON Schema keywords — no vendor brand survives stringify (#1835)
why: THE BRAND CAME BACK ONCE ALREADY. The original converter branded Zod's JSON Schema render with
`Type.Unsafe`, and the brand's clone made Zod's non-enumerable `~standard` metadata enumerable,
so every tool's parameters serialized with `~standard.{vendor,version}` and strict providers
refused the whole declaration. A converter can re-grow that wrapper for the best of reasons
(TSchema looks like it wants a TypeBox value), which is why the guard lives at the seam pi owns:
P1 RESTORES THE #1835 DEFECT VERBATIM, import and call in one span: re-introducing the call
without its `Type` import is a ReferenceError the suite dies in before any cell, an unrelated
red, so the mutation carries both halves of the pre-fix shape. It must redden the round-trip
cell, whose stray-path list is the direct measurement of the provider-facing leak; closure
cells stay green under it, exactly as they did at base — the defect is orthogonal to closure,
and a mutation that reddened a closure cell would be proving a different regression.
P2 IS THE SUBTLER RE-INTRODUCTION: not the brand, but an ordinary enumerable member smuggled
onto the render. It proves the cell walks ALL keys at every depth rather than matching the one
string `~standard` — a cell that special-cased yesterday's key name would pass the next
vendor's metadata member straight through to the provider.
NO BUILD STEP: the suite imports the extension's src through tsx and registers tools against a
fake ExtensionAPI, so there is no dist/ copy that could disagree with the mutation.

mutations.name: P1 the Type.Unsafe brand returns (the #1835 defect verbatim)
mutations.expectRed: a JSON round-trip of every tool's parameters carries ONLY JSON Schema keywords (22 tools)
mutations.cell: a JSON round-trip of every tool's parameters carries ONLY JSON Schema keywords (22 tools)
mutations.note: The code-only return-line mutation calls Type.Unsafe through Node’s built-in createRequire, so the fixture restores the exact branded shape without needing a second import edit or anchoring across comments. The brand’s clone makes Zod’s non-enumerable ~standard enumerable, so stringify carries parameters(cotal_*).~standard for all 22 tools and the round-trip cell names every path.

mutations.name: P2 an ordinary enumerable vendor member is smuggled onto the render
mutations.replace: return Object.assign(z.toJSONSchema(schema, { io: "input" }), { vendor: "zod" }) as TSchema;
mutations.expectRed: a JSON round-trip of every tool's parameters carries ONLY JSON Schema keywords (22 tools)
mutations.cell: a JSON round-trip of every tool's parameters carries ONLY JSON Schema keywords (22 tools)
mutations.note: A non-brand re-introduction: one enumerable key no JSON Schema defines, on every tool. Proves the cell grades key names against the vocabulary at all depths rather than matching the literal ~standard.

mutations.name: P3 the bounded continuation retry never fires (#726 defect verbatim)
mutations.replace:
this.hold(`${reasonLabel}; Cotal delivery is retained until a proven clean continuation completes`);
      return;
mutations.expectRed: the bounded continuation re-dispatches the exact retained batch content within the backoff window
mutations.cell: the bounded continuation re-dispatches the exact retained batch content within the backoff window
mutations.note: Restores the pre-#726 shape verbatim: a non-terminal error with a batch pending holds forever with no timer and no retry path, exactly the defect the issue reports (a turn nothing in the process can start). The acceptance cell's second host.sent assertion, which waits past the 50ms backoff for a second send, reddens because that send never happens.

mutations.name: P4 the attempt bound is removed (retries forever, never reaches intervention)
mutations.expectRed: the held reason names the spent attempt count
mutations.cell: the held reason names the spent attempt count
mutations.note: Removes the bound while keeping the retry itself: every non-terminal failure re-schedules a continuation forever, so the attempts-spent cell's two-failure loop never reaches the intervention hold and its heldReason regex against '2 automatic continuation attempts' reddens (the driver is still 'held' with the retrying-reason text, not the spent-attempts text).

mutations.name: P5 the intervention wording is dropped from the spent-attempts hold
mutations.find:
`${reasonLabel} after ${CONTINUATION_ATTEMPT_LIMIT} automatic continuation attempts; Cotal delivery ` +
          "needs intervention: start a new turn in this session, or replace the seat.",
mutations.replace: `${reasonLabel} after ${CONTINUATION_ATTEMPT_LIMIT} automatic continuation attempts; Cotal delivery is retained until a proven clean continuation completes.`,
mutations.expectRed: the held reason names intervention rather than promising a continuation
mutations.cell: the held reason names intervention rather than promising a continuation
mutations.note: Keeps the attempt bound and the attempt-count wording (the driver still stops retrying at the limit and still names the count) but reverts only the terminal clause back to the ordinary 'retained until a proven clean continuation completes' text, silently promising a continuation that will never come once the budget is spent. The attempts-spent cell's /intervention/i checks against both heldReason and the presence line redden, while the attempt-count assertion on the same line stays green, isolating the named cell.
